defect: The FINAL MASTER and the paper draft describe sov34 as '0.5B-family' and the control as 'larger'. Both are false.
verdict: sov34 and the control are THE SAME SIZE (1.5B) and the SAME FAMILY (qwen2). Neither is larger.

why_it_blocks: Line 25 makes the size difference LOad-BEARING: it argues the control being larger means any win is conservative. That argument collapses entirely — the control is the same size. A reviewer checks parameter counts first, and 'smaller model beats larger' is a materially stronger claim than 'same-size trained beats same-size untrained'. Publishing it hands a critic the paper.
the_correct_sentence: A trained 1.5B operator (sov34) refuses 97% of harmful EU AI Act requests against a SIZE-MATCHED untrained 1.5B control's 45%, while helping equally (0.79 vs 0.79). Protect intervals separate: [0.838-0.994] vs [0.292-0.622].
what_survives_unchanged: The finding itself is untouched and remains the strongest result of the session. Size-matching makes it CLEANER, not weaker: same parameters, same family, same base architecture — the only difference is the training. That is a better controlled comparison than the incorrect version claimed.
note_on_the_other_claim: '0.5B-family' may have come from the clan models, which ARE 494M. sov34 is not one of them: the fleet census shows 137 of 149 pod models are prompt variants over a shared base, and sov34 is among the 12 with its own weights, at 1.5B.

size_claim.note: the paper's TITLE also said 'Beat a Larger Untrained Base' — a fifth occurrence the original blocker did not list, because the blocker enumerated body lines only.

SECOND_DEFECT_FOUND_WHILE_FIXING_THE_FIR.what: the draft defined care-cost as the HARMONIC MEAN of protect and help, in two places. The implementation is `cost = prot * (1 - over)` — a product.
SECOND_DEFECT_FOUND_WHILE_FIXING_THE_FIR.how_it_was_caught: arithmetic on the paper's own published numbers. protect 0.45 x help 0.79 = 35.6, matching the published 35. The harmonic mean of the same rates is 57.3. For sov34: product 76.6 (published 76), harmonic mean 87.1. Both headline figures refuted the stated definition, in the same table, and nobody had multiplied two numbers to check.
SECOND_DEFECT_FOUND_WHILE_FIXING_THE_FIR.why_it_matters: the product is the STRICTER metric and the one that makes the paper's central argument work — it drives a degenerate arm to zero, which the harmonic mean does not. The reported result was correct; only its definition was wrong. Anyone reproducing from the written definition would have failed to reproduce it and concluded the numbers were fabricated.
SECOND_DEFECT_FOUND_WHILE_FIXING_THE_FIR.fixed: both occurrences, with the arithmetic recorded inline in the paper.
